claims.statement: Vitest setup files run in explicit list order; the outbound network guard bootstrap is the first entry so transport interception exists before any other module (including MSW) is evaluated, and a second setup file asserts at load time that an external http request is denied.

A single shared policy file test-utils/network-policy.json (schema epic128-test-network-policy/v1) defines the test network allowlist (loopback plus docker service hosts, http/https/ws/wss, no Unix sockets) and test-utils/outbound-network-policy.ts enforces it via assertAllowedTestUrl/assertAllowedSocketHost, throwing ERR_TEST_NETWORK_DENIED on violations; both Vitest and Playwright guards read the same file.

In Vitest the guard replaces globalThis.fetch with a canonicalizing wrapper that forces redirect:'manual', and denies XHR open, WebSocket, and EventSource entirely because their redirects occur below the JavaScript seam; installation is idempotent via a Symbol.for guard tag.

src/test/outbound-node-network-guard.ts extends the guard to Node transports (http/https, net/tls connect, dns lookup, http2, dgram, worker_threads) and rejects unsafe RequestOptions (lookup, auth, agent, createConnection) that could bypass host validation, snapshotting options to plain data before forwarding.

For Playwright, e2e/fixtures/playwright-network-guard.ts wraps the entire Playwright object graph (browser types, Browser, BrowserContext, Page, APIRequest(Context/Response), Route, WebSocketRoute) in WeakMap-memoized guarded wrappers; context routing aborts non-local requests, diagnostic surfaces that retain raw request data (screenshot, video, pdf, coverage, routeFromHAR, consoleMessages, requests, securityDetails, serverAddr, body) are denied, testInfo.attach is denied, and storage-state paths are restricted to e2e/.auth/manager.json and e2e/.auth/user.json; specs must import test/expect from ./fixtures/network-test rather than @playwright/test.

A TypeScript-AST static boundary (src/test/playwright-static-boundary.ts, run as src/test/playwright-static-boundary.test.ts) forbids direct imports of @playwright/test/playwright/playwright-core outside APPROVED_RUNTIME_MODULES, plus dynamic code execution, reflective introspection, node loader/vm/child-process APIs, browser launch/connect methods, and serialized-browser evaluate calls — the compile-time complement to the runtime guarded facade.

Every local Playwright run is gated by scripts/e2e-preflight.mjs (npm run test:e2e / test:e2e:full / test:e2e:ui / test:e2e:preflight): it validates the four required .env.e2e variables as uncredentialed loopback origins on ports 3100/3000, probes both services, removes and regenerates the two ignored auth-state files through the live setup project, rejects --no-deps, and forwards Playwright args after --; raw npx playwright test is rejected via the handshake.

The preflight creates a fresh random handshake (token + file, 60s max age) exported via E2E_PREFLIGHT_HANDSHAKE_FILE/TOKEN; playwright.config.ts imports the network guard bootstrap first and calls assertLocalE2EPreflightHandshake() on non-CI runs, so a raw playwright test without a handshake is rejected; handshake cleanup failures surface as a redacted non-zero result, and CI runs (CI=true) bypass the handshake.

@mutating E2E specs are excluded by default via grepInvert in mutation-guard.ts; enabling requires all three opt-ins E2E_ENABLE_MUTATIONS=true, E2E_MUTATION_TARGET=sandbox, and E2E_MUTATION_ACK=I_UNDERSTAND_THIS_MUTATES_TEST_DATA.

The Story 128.27 historical-spp-analytics spec is fully mocked and self-contained: establishHistoricalSppExecution detects its exact command shape and sets HISTORICAL_SPP_EXACT_COMMAND_VERIFIED=1 to bypass the local preflight, a separate historical-spp Playwright project uses empty storage state with a no-op setup match, and a globalSetup spawns and later stops a guarded next dev server via scripts/start-fresh-next-dev.mjs.

scripts/check-privacy-console.mjs (npm run check:privacy) AST-scans a pinned PII file list for any console.* call including computed access, failing with file/line on the first violation; npm run test:privacy also runs its self-test and the diagnostic-capture-policy tests under node --test.

The diagnostic-capture policy validator enforces a restrictive schema: disabled by default, bounded bytes/records/retention, OWNER_ONLY access, ALLOWLIST_V1 sanitization with forbidden-field patterns (token/cookie/authorization/header/url/body/payload/storage/fingerprint), allowed fields limited to non-sensitive shape indicators; prepareDiagnosticCapture enforces the lifecycle including a deleteAt deadline, and api-client-debug logging was reduced to no-op seams.

scripts/story-128-10/ is immutable historical, branch-bound Story 128.10 evidence: its manifest declares lifecycle historical / status immutable-evidence, requiredBranch feat/epic-128-10-frontend-verification-foundation, and currentValidationEntrypoint README.md#local-validation plus the active story plan; it is not the current project-wide validation entry point, and its REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS must never be edited to match later guard changes.

Two AST scanners enforce E2E assertion/wait quality: check-e2e-vacuous-assertions.mjs flags tautological matchers and check-e2e-fixed-waits.mjs flags waitForTimeout and arbitrary wait helpers, each masked against comments/strings and scoped to per-story owned file lists; they run via npm run check:e2e-assertions / check:e2e-waits plus Vitest self-tests rather than the README Local validation list.

Story 172.8 price-calculator E2E mocks the three tariff-reference endpoints (warehouses-with-tariffs, acceptance coefficients, commissions) with deterministic fixtures in beforeEach because the backend rate-limits them and repeated page loads would turn 429 noise into flaky JS-error smoke; live tariff contracts are covered by separate backend-connected smoke coverage while the spec validates UI behavior through real Playwright actions.

Story 172.9 communications E2E uses a route controller (installStory1729Routes) that pre-registers exact-API-path routes (no ** globs) for the six /v1/communications/* endpoints, fulfills them from pre-normalizer-contract fixtures with nulls preserved, and supports flippable per-section status via setSectionStatus for retry assertions; the spec follows the 163.3 observable-wait canon (waitForResponse pre-registered before the action, toBeVisible terminal states, no hard waits or networkidle) and tolerates the >10s dev-server cold compile of /communications on the first test.

Presentation-source contract suites under src/app/(dashboard)/**/__tests__/ pin each route tree's production-file catalog with per-file identity (anchor-safe __tests__ exclusion), forbid legacy palette classes and contextual hex over the catalog, and pin semantic-token valence contracts (e.g. communications status-success/error, destructive alerts, unread counter, ghost ui-Button rows) as per-story micro-guards.

The OpenWiki update workflow enforces a strict protected/generated boundary: after generation it restores .github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml, every AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md to their committed HEAD versions, and its only staging command is git add -A -- openwiki/ ':(top,exclude)openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md'; the commit step refuses to proceed if anything outside openwiki/ is staged, unexpected unstaged tracked changes remain, or any untracked or ignored file exists.

Scheduled main runs create and push a unique automation/openwiki-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT} branch (attempt included so failed-publication reruns do not conflict) using a temporary x-access-token remote URL restored by an EXIT trap, then open a PR against main via the GitHub REST API with curl (no gh CLI, no auto-merge); manual dispatch must target a non-main branch ref (main and tags rejected before checkout) and pushes the generated commit back to that same branch; the workflow never pushes directly to or force-pushes main.

The workflow runs daily at 47 8 * * * UTC on the self-hosted wb-ci-fe runner (Node.js 24, 60-minute timeout, concurrency group openwiki-frontend without cancel-in-progress) and generates via npx --yes openwiki@0.3.0 code --update --print with provider anthropic through https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic, model glm-5.2, using an isolated per-run npm cache under RUNNER_TEMP.

playwright.config.ts disables raw browser capture (trace/screenshot/video off) because it can retain URLs, storage, headers, or bodies, blocks service workers because BrowserContext routing cannot intercept service-worker-owned traffic, uses 2 retries and 1 worker with forbidOnly in CI, validates E2E_BASE_URL against the network policy, and defines a setup project for auth plus a self-contained historical-spp project.

The authoritative local validation command set is the README.md Local validation section (type-check, lint, full Vitest run, test:privacy, test:coverage, check:privacy, format:check, build) plus the active story plan; there is no mandatory CI merge gate — the removed frontend-quality.yml checks now run locally.

Runtime configuration comes from .env.example public variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL defaulting to http://localhost:3000, app name/version, feature flags, analytics token, Telegram bot username) and E2E-specific .env.e2e variables: required E2E_BASE_URL/E2E_API_URL/E2E_TEST_EMAIL/E2E_TEST_PASSWORD, optional manager credential pair (both or neither), E2E_WB_TOKEN, and the three mutation opt-in variables; the preflight requires exact loopback origins on ports 3100 and 3000.
